title: Courtade-Kumar one-bit information bound: exact finite checks, analytic controls and local-rule readouts
setting: X uniform on {0,1}^n (n independent fair bits); Y = X xor Z with Z i.i.d. Bernoulli(p) (BSC); f a deterministic one-bit function of X; quantity I(f(X); Y) in bits, exact by enumeration
bound_under_test: I(f(X);Y) <= 1 - h2(p) for 0 <= p <= 1/2 (finite numerical checks only; the general theorem is not proven here)

analytic_controls.parity_k: f = parity of the first k bits (k = 2 and k = n): I = 1 - h2((1 - (1 - 2p)^k) / 2)
analytic_controls.majority: odd n only: computed, no closed form; must respect the bound

candidate_readouts: Elementary cellular-automaton rules 0-255 on a ring of n cells, T in {1, 2, 3} synchronous steps, readout = cell 0; only readouts whose truth table depends on at least two input bits are eligible (single-bit functions attain the bound trivially)
selection: Choose the eligible (rule, T) with the highest mean efficiency I / (1 - h2(p)) over p_dev at n = 8; ties: lowest rule, then lowest T; TEST p values are never used for selection

endpoints.E1: number of evaluated (function, n, p) cases with I > 1 - h2(p) + 1e-12 (expected 0)
endpoints.E2: maximum absolute deviation of analytic controls from their closed forms (tolerance 1e-12)
endpoints.E3: efficiency of the selected readout at each p_test and n = 8 (descriptive)
endpoints.E4: distribution checks: the joint distribution sums to 1 and Y is uniform, within 1e-12
endpoints.E5: agreement between the vectorized evaluator and completion_kit.dynamics.boolean_noise_information on 300 registered random cases (tolerance 1e-12)

scope_limits: Not applied to ten-class labels, UCI images, spatial dropout or dependent neural states
Any extension is a new hypothesis that needs its own proof
